remarks.name: Guillermo Rauch
remarks.role: vercel CEO
remarks.text:
Next.js 16.3: faster, better, stronger. My highlights:

0️⃣ Faster dev & builds
Shoutout to Fable for improving memory use, and the team for landing the incremental 𝚗𝚎𝚡𝚝 𝚋𝚞𝚒𝚕𝚍 cache.

1️⃣ Instant navigations are 🔥
The people wanted SPAs, they shall get SPAs. By turning on instant navs (which will soon be default), your  agent is basically forced to make things fast.

2️⃣ Agent-native DX
You can still ship "slow" navs if you want, e.g. by blocking navs on server-side data fetching ala PHP olden days. But even then, your agent will be given *choices*, like setting up a <𝚂𝚞𝚜𝚙𝚎𝚗𝚜𝚎 𝚏𝚊𝚕𝚕𝚋𝚊𝚌𝚔> for instant loading shells. Agents also get built-in versioned docs.

This is our best release for agents by far, which will also make your upgrading journey very smooth. I've had an easy time bumping my projects to 16.3 and enabling instant navs, having my agent migrate everything without issues.

And so much more. 16.3 is more cost-efficient to serve, both in self-hosting and serverless environments. Faster to type-check… Thank you to the 90 contributors to this release!
remarks.translation: Next.js 16.3：更快、更好、更强。我的亮点：0️⃣ 更快的开发与构建速度 感谢 Fable 改进了内存使用，以及团队实现了增量 𝚗𝚎𝚡𝚝 𝚋𝚞𝚒𝚕𝚍 缓存。1️⃣ 即时导航体验 🔥 用户想要单页应用，他们就该得到单页应用。开启即时导航（很快将成为默认设置）后，你的智能体基本上就被迫让一切变快。2️⃣ 面向智能体的开发体验 如果你愿意，仍然可以保留“慢速”导航，比如像 PHP 老式做法那样，在服务端数据获取时阻塞导航。但即便如此，你的智能体也会获得*选择权*，例如设置 <𝚂𝚞𝚜𝚙𝚎𝚗𝚜𝚎 𝚏𝚊𝚕𝚕𝚋𝚊𝚌𝚔> 来实现即时加载骨架。智能体还能获得内置的版本化文档。这是迄今为止我们为智能体打造的最佳版本，也会让你的升级过程非常顺畅。我轻松地将自己的项目升级到了 16.3 并启用了即时导航，让我的智能体毫无问题地完成了所有迁移工作。还有更多亮点。16.3 在服务成本上更高效，无论是自托管还是无服务器环境。类型检查也更快……感谢本次发布的 90 位贡献者！

remarks.name: Peter Yang
remarks.role: Practical AI tutorials and interviews for busy people
remarks.text:
“For us, we just want open source to win at the end of the day. We want freedom to happen for people.”

You can hear the passion for open source in this clip from my interview with @karan4d, @NousResearch co-founder:

“We need to give this level of intelligence to everyone so they can be on an even and equal playing field.”

Karan's vision for Hermes is to give everyone access to intelligent AI, then let each person shape it into an agent that’s uniquely theirs.

📌 Watch the full episode here: https://t.co/3E7IC0TzNr
remarks.translation: “对我们来说，归根结底，我们只希望开源能够获胜。我们希望自由能够降临到每个人身上。”在我对@karan4d（@NousResearch联合创始人）的采访中，可以听到他对开源的这份热忱：“我们需要将这种水平的智能赋予每一个人，让他们都能站在公平平等的起跑线上。”Karan对Hermes的愿景是让每个人都能获得智能AI，然后让每个人将其塑造成独一无二、专属于自己的智能体。📌 在此观看完整剧集：https://t.co/3E7IC0TzNr

remarks.text:
Even though I try to make sure to say bye to my kids before I go to work,

some days have me crawling out of my house on all fours quietly like a thief so they don’t bawl when they see me leaving. 

And you learn all about which doors (and drawers) are squeaky and fixing them stat so your crime goes silently unpunished. 

The little one has gotten surprisingly good at intercepting these maneuvers intuitively and will need to update my tactics!
remarks.translation: 尽管我努力确保上班前跟孩子们道别，但有些日子我不得不像小偷一样悄悄爬出家门，免得他们看到我离开时嚎啕大哭。你会摸清哪些门（和抽屉）会吱吱作响，并立刻修好它们，好让你的“罪行”悄无声息地不被发现。小家伙已经出奇地擅长凭直觉拦截这些招数了，看来我得更新我的战术了！

podcasts.name: Training Data (Sequoia)
podcasts.title: Chai Discovery的苦涩教训：药物设计是另一个扩展问题
podcasts.originalTitle: Chai Discovery's Bitter Lesson: Drug Design Is Another Scaling Problem
podcasts.excerpt: 多数人将生物学视为一门定制化、杂乱无章的科学。Chai Discovery 联合创始人乔希·迈尔和马特·麦克帕特隆却将其当作工程问题来处理。他们论证，药物设计遵循着那条苦涩的教训：只要规模化数据、模型和算力，模型就能学到手工构建的流程根本无法捕捉的东西。成果实实在在：Chai-2 将从头抗体设计的命中率从不足 0.1% 提升到了 16%，把大海捞针式的搜索变成了更像配钥匙开锁的过程。乔希提出一个反直觉的观点：生物学比代码更容易验证，并解释了为什么目标应该是做更多而非更少的实验室实验。他们的赌注是：打造一个设计套件，将药物发现周期从九个月压缩到九天，并为制药行业赋能，而非与之竞争。主持人为红杉资本的帕特·格雷迪和索娜莉·辛格。 00:00 引言 01:52 从发现到设计 03:25 专…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Most people treat biology as a bespoke, messy science. Josh Meier and Matt McPartlon, co-founders of Chai Discovery, treat it as an engineering problem. They make the case that drug design obeys the bitter lesson: scale data, models, and compute, and the model can learn what a hand-built pipeline simply couldn't capture. The results are concrete: Chai-2 pushed de novo antibody design from a sub 0.1% hit rate to 16%, turning a needle-in-a-haystack search into something more like designing a key to fit a lock. Josh argues, counterintuitively, that biology is more verifiable than code, and explains why the goal should be more lab experiments, not fewer. Their bet: a design suite that collapses drug discovery from nine months to nine days, and arms the pharma industry rather than competing with it. podcasts.title: 第90集：AI先驱尤尔根·施密德胡伯谈当今AI现状
podcasts.originalTitle: Ep 90: AI Pioneer Jürgen Schmidhuber on the State of AI Today
podcasts.excerpt: 德高望重的科学家、AI 研究员于尔根·施密德胡伯博士被公认为该领域的先驱之一，他通过其实验室的工作，提出了当今 Transformer、LSTM 和递归自我改进背后的关键思想。他认为，真正的通用人工智能（AGI）仍受限于物理硬件，随着开源技术追赶封闭实验室的步伐，当今对 AI 数据中心的投资将迎来调整，而通往通用智能的道路在于人工好奇心与自主生成的实验，而非互联网数据。最后，他重新审视了主流的 AI 安全论点，并描绘了一幅自我复制的机器人社会最终殖民太阳系的宏大愿景。（0:00）引言（1:24）超人类 AI 还有多远？（2:27）ChatGPT 为何未让他感到意外（3:21）递归自我改进之路（9:01）AI 会起飞吗……
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Dr. Jürgen Schmidhuber, a renowned scientist and AI researcher widely regarded as one of the pioneers in the field, originated key ideas behind today's transformers, LSTMs, and recursive self-improvement through his lab's work. He argues that true AGI remains bottlenecked by physical hardware, that today's AI data center investments are headed for a correction as open-source keeps pace with closed labs, and that the path to general intelligence runs through artificial curiosity and self-generated experimentation rather than internet data. He closes by reconsidering mainstream AI safety arguments and offers a sweeping vision of self-replicating robot societies eventually colonizing the solar system. podcasts.name: Unsupervised Learning (Redpoint)
podcasts.title: 第91集：顶级AI分析师解析当今AI炒作周期
podcasts.originalTitle: Ep 91: Top AI Analyst Unpacks Today's AI Hype Cycle
podcasts.excerpt: 科技界最受瞩目的分析师之一本尼迪克特·埃文斯做客雅各布·埃夫隆的节目。对话围绕本尼迪克特的核心论点展开：将人工智能的规模与过往平台变革（互联网、移动互联网、个人电脑）相类比，在分析层面毫无意义；更具建设性的做法是，研究那些技术在经济层面的实际演进过程，从而推断人工智能的价值将沉淀在何处。他认为，这次真正的不同在于，我们不知道人工智能的物理或科学边界，而过往变革中这些边界至少是可预知的——正是这种不确定性，既催生了通用人工智能的狂热，也助长了末日论调，却无法解决任何实质问题。本尼迪克特深入剖析了为何能力仍呈锯齿状分布，这意味着使用场景同样参差不齐；为何编程凭借可规模化验证的特性，成为首个真正的企业级应用场景；以及为何大多数消费级和企业级应用场景，仍有待创业者去发明……
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Benedict Evans, one of tech's most widely-read analysts, joins Jacob Effron. The conversation centers on Benedict's core thesis that comparing AI's scale to past platform shifts (the internet, mobile, PCs) is analytically useless, and that the more productive move is studying how those previous technologies actually evolved economically to reason about where AI's value will accrue. He argues the one genuine difference this time is that we don't know AI's physical or scientific limits, unlike past shifts where the boundaries were at least knowable, and that this uncertainty is what fuels both AGI hype and doomerism without resolving anything. Benedict unpacks why capabilities remain jagged, meaning usage is jagged too, why coding became the first real enterprise use case thanks to scalable verification, and why most consumer and enterprise use cases still have to be invented by entrepreneurs rat…
